prompt.context: Our client is an international manufacturer of medium and high quality kitchen knives. Chef's Best sells knives in more than 20 countries, with a focus on Latin America, US & Canada, and global emerging economies. Chef's Best produces five types of knives: Steak Knives (used at the table), Butcher Knives (used for chopping meat), Carving Knives (used for carving slices from large pieces of meat), Paring Knives (used for cutting small fruits & vegetables), and Chef's Knives (large all purpose knives). Chef's Best has experienced slowing sales growth in the past few years.
prompt.question: How can Chef's Best increase revenue growth for the next 5-10 years?

clarifying_info.q: How does Chef's Best sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Chef's Best sells primarily through a direct sales method — individual sales people throughout each region.
Chef's Best sales are largest in Mexico, the US, and Brazil.

exhibits.title: Overview of Major Markets
exhibits.shows: A chart displaying growth rates and profitability metrics across Chef's Best major geographic markets, with footnotes defining an index-to-market calculation.
exhibits.data: Includes market growth rates and Chef's Best growth rates by country; footnote defines index to market as (Chef's Best growth / market growth - 1) * 100; Mexico market growth ~7%, Chef's Best index to market = -70; Chef's Best current market share in Mexico = 23%

exhibits.title: Overview of Product Categories
exhibits.shows: A chart comparing Chef's Best performance across the five knife product categories, showing market share and distribution channel metrics for each category.
exhibits.data: Shows share changes and channel metrics for Steak Knives, Butcher Knives, Carving Knives, Paring Knives, and Chef's Knives; Butcher Knives show both channel and market share losses

exhibits.title: Details of Butcher Knives Category
exhibits.shows: A detailed breakdown of the Butcher Knives category including overall category growth rate, sales by distribution channel (retail vs. direct sales), and performance by knife sub-type (Recycled Steel, Japanese, General Purpose).
exhibits.data: High overall category growth rate; majority of current sales through direct sales channel; retail distribution represents a significant untapped opportunity; sub-types include Recycled Steel, Japanese, and General Purpose

framework: Market: Market size and growth across geographies, product segments, and customer segments
Competition: New players capturing share via better distribution or marketing; low-cost competitors; substitutes such as electronic choppers and food processors
Customer: Segmentation (e.g., chef's knives for restaurants vs. households); price sensitivity
Product: Product mix alignment with consumer preferences; complementary products and services; quality and brand image
Company: Distribution channel coverage and gaps; cross-selling effectiveness across knife types; sales force effectiveness

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 1 tell you about Chef's Best performance, and what are the key implications?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Mexico and Brazil as the largest profit centers; flag that Mexico shows poor growth (index to market of -70 meaning Chef's Best grew far below the market rate); distinguish risk areas (Mexico share loss) from growth opportunities; draw confident conclusions about where to focus and where the business is at risk.

math.setup: If Chef's Best has 23% market share in Mexico and grows at the same rate as last year, what will market share be in 1 year? Mexico market grows at 7%; Chef's Best index to market = -70. Use the index formula: Index = (Chef's Best growth rate / market growth rate - 1) * 100.
steps: Solve for Chef's Best growth rate: -70/100 = (x/7) - 1 => -0.7 + 1 = x/7 => 0.3 = x/7 => x = 2.1% growth
math.answer: 21.9% market share in Mexico after one year

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 2 reveal about the drivers of Chef's Best market share changes?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify that Chef's Best is losing share across all product categories; highlight that Butcher Knives stand out with losses in both channel metrics and market share — making it the highest-priority focus area; prioritize categories and channels for remediation.

questions.prompt: What does Exhibit 3 tell you about the Butcher Knives category, and what should Chef's Best do?
questions.guidance: Candidate should note the high overall growth rate in the Butcher Knives category (explaining why the market share loss in Exhibit 2 is particularly costly); acknowledge the significant potential of the retail distribution channel vs. the current direct sales model which dominates current sales; develop recommendations to invest in Butcher Knives, expand retail distribution, and focus specifically on growing Recycled Steel, Japanese, and General Purpose sub-types; connect back to earlier exhibits to build a broader set of recommendations.

brainstorming.prompt: How would you approach the problem of increasing revenue growth for Chef's Best over the next 5-10 years? Walk me through your framework.

categories.name: Market
ideas: Assess size and growth rates across all 20+ countries
Identify fastest-growing emerging markets for expansion
Analyze product segment growth trends (which knife types are growing?)
Identify customer segment opportunities (professional chefs, restaurants, households)

categories.name: Competition
ideas: Identify new entrants capturing share through better distribution or lower prices
Assess threat of substitutes (food processors, electronic choppers)
Benchmark Chef's Best pricing vs. competitors in each market
Evaluate competitor marketing effectiveness

categories.name: Customer
ideas: Segment customers by use case (professional vs. home cook)
Understand price sensitivity across segments
Identify underserved customer segments
Explore bundling or complementary product opportunities (e.g., knife sets, sharpeners)

categories.name: Product
ideas: Evaluate whether product mix matches consumer preferences by market
Assess quality perception and brand image
Explore complementary products (knife blocks, sharpeners, cutting boards)
Consider premium vs. value product line extensions

categories.name: Company / Distribution
ideas: Expand beyond direct sales to retail distribution channels
Assess sales force coverage and effectiveness across regions
Identify cross-selling opportunities across knife types
Evaluate e-commerce and digital channels
Consider partnerships with restaurant supply chains

recommendation: Focus on growing share in Mexico and the US to retain the core business and prevent further share and scale economy losses to competitors
Invest in emerging markets but recognize that the top 3 markets (Mexico, US, Brazil) represent ~60% of sales and must be protected
Invest in the Butcher Knives category to expand distribution and address marketing weaknesses given its high growth rate
Begin shifting the business model away from the costlier direct sales channel toward retail distribution to capture untapped growth potential and reduce cost-to-serve
risks: A shift in sales method toward retail may require reducing direct sales headcount — layoff plans and change management must be addressed proactively
Historical trends in market growth or share may not continue; competitive and macro dynamics can change
next_steps: Open negotiations with retail distributors to identify pathways to expanded distribution, particularly for Butcher Knives
Conduct a competitive analysis in Mexico and the US to pinpoint specific causes of below-market share growth
Prepare financial plans and investment cases for increasing spend behind the Butcher Knives category, especially Recycled Steel, Japanese, and General Purpose sub-types
